- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) or shows strong negative momentum, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >7% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements — apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.2 in 3-day window), model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- If model forecast is below 65.0 and sentiment is positive, add 0.5–1.0% to avoid “panic” underestimation.
- If model forecast is above 72.0 and sentiment is negative, reduce by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence in upside.
